detail.title: Overfitted, Underfitted, and Well-Fitted Models
detail.description: Given training and testing confusion matrices for three models of varying complexity: (1) fill in the TP/TN/FP/FN definitions; (2) complete the accuracy table to two decimals; (3) state whether each model was overfitted, well-fitted or underfitted, whether it fit the training data, and whether it predicted the test data well.
detail.understand: Compare each model's training and test accuracy. The matrices total 319 (training) and 81 (testing) — the same sizes as carseats_train/test. Layout: rows = Actual, columns = Predicted; positive = 1.

questions.prompt: Fill in: TP, TN, FP, FN in terms of Predicted and Actual.
Classify Model 1, 2, 3 as overfitted / well-fitted / underfitted.

detail.interpretation: Model 1 has the best training accuracy but loses the most on test data (overfitted). Model 2 generalizes best (well-fitted). Model 3 predicts '1' for everything, so its accuracy is just the share of 1s (underfitted).
common_mistakes: Calling Model 3 'well-fitted' because train and test accuracy are equal — equal but poor means underfitted.
Choosing the model with the best training accuracy.
Reading the matrix as Predicted × Actual (that is Table 8.3's layout, not this one's).
notes: Matrices transcribed from the DS4A p.401 image and checked: training totals 319, testing totals 81.

answers.explanation: Positive = 1. 'True/False' says whether the prediction was right; 'Positive/Negative' is what was predicted.
Accuracy = sum of the diagonal / total (DS4A Quick Tip).

model_1.label: overfitted
model_1.reason: it has the highest training accuracy (0.80) but its test accuracy (0.64) is lower than model 2's; the gap of 0.15 shows it memorised training details.

model_2.label: well-fitted
model_2.reason: it has the highest test accuracy (0.65) and a small train-test gap (0.06).

model_3.label: underfitted
model_3.reason: training accuracy 0.59 is no better than always predicting the majority class (0.59) — it predicts the same class for every observation; test accuracy 0.59 is equally poor.

answers.explanation: Overfitted: good on training, worse on test. Well-fitted: good on both. Underfitted: poor on both (DS4A p.387).
